title: Can equal lengths still collapse?
hook: Can lengths survive while two points collapse together?

claims.text:
stage computation: Points O=(0,0,0), A=e1,B=e2,C=e3. Project with the signed matrix R0=[[1,1,1],[1,−1,1]]/sqrt2. R1=[[1,1,−1],[1,−1,1]]/sqrt2 is a second declared draw. Compute all six original/projected Euclidean distances and their ratios. R0 collapses A/C from sqrt2 to0; R1 preserves their sqrt2 distance but stretches B/C from sqrt2 to2.

**Countercase / boundary:** The matrices are explicit labelled draws0/1 from the finite sign-matrix family; no claim that these two outcomes establish a high-probability dimensional bound. Every projected column has unit length, yet some pairs collapse. Do not call2D a JL-guaranteed target dimension for these examples.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict whether equal column norms guarantee pairwise preservation; recall original O–A distance1 remains1 under either draw while A–C can fail.

**Intervention / reachable witness:** Draw choice recomputes point positions and a selected pair’s original/projected lengths; retain the collapsed-pair witness when switching draw. Enumerate the matrix entries, not an unexplained “seed” button.
